# My year on the land

Aiyo, let me think. I'm getting the seeds and fertilizer ready now. Cotton is the first big job — got to get it in the ground by late April. Wheat is already up in the field, I planted it last October like always. Maize comes later, after the wheat comes off in June.

## My 6.5 mu

I split my land like I always have. About 4 mu I do wheat then maize, same as my mother-in-law taught me thirty years back. The other 2.5 mu I keep in cotton — it brings in cash money even if the work is hard on my back.

## Wheat (4 mu, already planted)

Last October I put down one bag of compound fertilizer for each mu before I sowed — that's the number all of us in the village use, my man brought it on the three-wheeler from the township. I used seed I saved from last year's harvest, mixed with a little new seed my cousin gave me.

Now the wheat is getting tall. In a couple weeks when it's at the jointing, I'll spread about half a bag of urea per mu — that's when the wheat really wants to eat. I'll pump water from the well two times, once around the topdressing and once when the grain is filling up. Water is expensive now, they meter it, so I don't waste it. If I see the little black bugs on the leaves or the weeds get bad, I'll mix some spray, but only if I see it — no point buying poison I don't need. Harvest comes first week of June. I hire the combine man from the next village, costs me some but I can't cut 4 mu by hand anymore, my knees.

Last year I got about 400 kg per mu. I'm hoping for the same.

## Maize (4 mu, after wheat)

The minute the wheat comes off, we've got to move fast. Maybe 3-4 days between wheat harvest and maize planting. I buy the hybrid seed from the shop in town — the same kind my neighbor Zhang's wife bought last year because hers did real well. Costs more than saved seed but maize hybrid you can't save, everybody knows.

I broadcast one bag of compound per mu at planting, then when the maize is about knee-high I side-dress maybe half a bag of urea. Spray once for the weeds right after planting — have to, or the weeds eat the baby plants. If July is dry I'll pump water once, maybe twice. Harvest end of September. Usually get about 450 kg per mu.

## Cotton (2.5 mu)

Cotton is where the money is but it's the hardest. I plant mid-April with the plastic film, my husband and me stretch the film together. Hybrid seed from the shop, same one I've used three years now because it gives good fiber.

Cotton eats a lot. I put down more than a bag of compound per mu before planting, then urea when it starts flowering. The bollworm is the worry — I'll spray three, maybe four times through the summer, whenever I see the holes in the leaves. My daughter-in-law helps me walk the rows. Pump water twice if the weather is hot.

Picking starts end of September and goes through October, sometimes into November. That's when I call my sister to come from her village to help. My hands hurt by the end but cotton pays.

Last year I got about 230 jin of lint per mu.

## What I worry about

Money for inputs — I have to buy cotton fertilizer and pesticide in spring before I've sold anything, so I count the yuan carefully. If the cotton price drops at harvest, I feel it for the whole year. And the weather — if no rain in May when the cotton is young, I have to pump a lot and that eats the profit. But this is how I've always done it and my family has eaten.
